subject: Dedicated capacity playbook — identified gaps for Q3 pilot
messages:
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-10T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity playbook — gaps identified for AquaHealth Q3 pilot

Kimberly — quick note from the product side after yesterday's sync.

We ran the pilot checklist against AquaHealth's expected traffic pattern and found two areas where the dedicated capacity playbook doesn't map cleanly to the ask: 

- Autoscale exception timing: the current exception policy requires a 72h lead and approval from Capacity Governance for >24h carveouts. AquaHealth needs a 36h pre-warm window for their nightly heavy scoring job.
- Reservation validity and billing alignment: procurement is asking for a formal reservation window + a fallback to shared capacity if thresholds are exceeded; finance also wants unit economics in the doc.

Can we get ops & finance guidance on whether a temporary 36h pre-warm carveout is acceptable and what approval path would look like? If not, product will push for a software-level mitigation (KV prefix pre-warm).

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Product Manager, Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-10T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity playbook — gaps identified for AquaHealth Q3 pilot

Laura — appreciate the flag. Short answers up front: we can support a 36h pre-warm, but it needs an exceptions workflow tweak and a one-off approval from Capacity Governance + Finance signoff for cost exposure.

Please action items below: 

- Marissa: can you run a quick cost delta for 36h pre-warm (expected GPU-hours + estimated token volume) and attach to the approval packet?
- Marcus: ops needs a minimal runbook change so on-call knows the fallback behavior (shared pool fallback + throttling thresholds). Can you draft a two-page ops appendix?
- Laura: I'll coordinate with Governance and Finance once we have the numbers; also please capture product mitigations (prefix cache) as a fallback.

I want to keep this light-touch — goal is approval within 24h so we don't delay AquaHealth's onboarding calendar.

Thanks,
Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Dedicated Capacity Programs
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-10T13:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity playbook — gaps identified for AquaHealth Q3 pilot

Attaching a quick spreadsheet summary and the first-pass playbook draft. Numbers are elastic and conservative. Highlights: 

- 36h pre-warm estimate: 18 GPU-hours (A100 equivalent) at baseline utilization; add 35% buffer for burst windows = ~24 GPU-hours.
- Estimated incremental cost to Redwood (unit compute + buffer): $4,100. If we bill AquaHealth pro-rata for the reservation window, net exposure drops to $900.

I've attached: capacity_playbook_v1.pdf (playbook with suggested exception step), ops_runbook_draft.md (two-page ops appendix), and a short costing CSV.

Next steps per Kimberly: 
- Finance approval for exposure or pricing proposal to procurement
- Governance exception note (I can draft)
- Ops appendix review by Marcus

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Strategic Account Lead 
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: capacity_playbook_v1.pdf]
[Attachment: ops_runbook_draft.md]
From: ops@aquahealth.com <ops@aquahealth.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@aquahealth.com <procurement@aquahealth.com>
Date: 2027-06-11T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity playbook — AquaHealth Q3 schedule constraints

Kimberly / team — thanks for the quick coordination. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- The 36h pre-warm is non-negotiable for our nightly scoring pipeline (regulatory SLA). We can accept a small pro-rated fee for the reservation window; procurement will need the exact numbers to issue an amendment.
- If we must rely on shared fallback, please confirm throttling guarantees and whether any token loss or truncation is possible under fallback.

Procurement is available for a short call this afternoon if that helps speed the formal sign-off.

Regards,
Anil Rao
Platform Ops Lead
AquaHealth
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@aquahealth.com <ops@aquahealth.com>, procurement@aquahealth.com <procurement@aquahealth.com>
Date: 2027-06-11T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity playbook — gaps identified for AquaHealth Q3 pilot

Team — summary and owner assignments to close the exception in 24h: 

- Finance & Pricing: Marissa to propose a pro-rated amendment amount (Marissa -> procurement number) and call out net exposure; target: send to procurement within 3 hours.
- Governance: Kimberly will submit formal exception request (INFRA-2287) referencing the playbook draft; ask: one-time 36h pre-warm carveout for onboarding.
- Ops: Marcus to review ops_runbook_draft.md and confirm fallback throttling thresholds (suggested default: 80% shared-pool throttle at 2x sustained baseline).
- Product: Laura to provide a short description of the KV prefix mitigation and expected effectiveness (50–70% cold-start reduction).

If we hit these actions we can approve the exception and publish the playbook patch. I'll host a 30-minute decision call at 19:00 PT today if anyone wants to join (calendar invite to follow).

I'll also attach the playbook and ops appendix into the governance ticket and link to the Drive folder.

Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Dedicated Capacity Programs
Redwood Inference
